turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST SHG
tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
I prioritized candidates that are structural/chemical analogs of the highest-SHG training entries: acentric chalcogenide/pnictide frameworks with heavy polarizable atoms (Te/Se/As), Hg/Cd/In/Tl-type cations, and chalcopyrite/wurtzite/Zintl-like motifs. I down-weighted alkali/alkaline-earth halides, Cl/Br/I-rich phases, and highly symmetric or alkali-rich structures, which are mostly low in the training set.

The strongest pool matches are heavy Te/Se/As-bearing analogs of high-training families: Cd–In–Te–As, Ba–Ge–Te/Se, Al–Hg–Se chalcopyrite-like, K–Ta–As Zintl analog of K14Nb2As8, and ordered Al/Ga arsenide.

Final: c073, c079, c082, c090, c055
